question: In a child with heat stroke (temperature >40°C, confusion, absence of sweating), the priority is the same as for fever — oral paracetamol 15 mg/kg and removal of clothing.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is FALSE. Heat stroke is NOT managed like fever. Antipyretics (paracetamol) are ineffective in heat stroke because the hypothalamic set-point is normal — the problem is a failure of heat dissipation, not a raised set-point. Heat stroke (>40°C + CNS dysfunction + anhidrosis) requires immediate aggressive physical cooling: cool water immersion or spray-and-fan, ice packs to neck/axillae/groin, and cold IV fluids. This is a life-threatening emergency.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is FALSE. Heat stroke is a thermoregulatory emergency distinct from fever. Fever results from a raised hypothalamic set-point and responds to antipyretics (paracetamol). Heat stroke involves a failure of thermoregulation with temperatures >40°C, CNS dysfunction, and anhidrosis — antipyretics do NOT work because the hypothalamic set-point is not elevated. Management = IMMEDIATE physical cooling (cool water immersion/spray + fanning, ice packs to axillae and groin, cold IV fluids) plus airway protection. Paracetamol is ineffective and should not be the priority.
